patch.value: Managed npm update checks report a subprocess timeout as npm_registry_lookup_failed, and the fixed 10 s npm view budget makes the Windows nightly extension-freshness test flaky

Nightly run 44087418672 (GitHub alert issue 1747, windows-latest Node 24 shard 4/4) failed tests/integration/extensions/extension-diagnostic-purity.integration.spec.ts in both the initial attempt and the retry (21.6 s for two attempts) at its first registry-backed freshness check: update_check_status was failed instead of checked. The test passes in 5.3 s on green Windows nights (run 43867277935) while spawning npm view several times, so each failing attempt spent the full GITHUB_UPDATE_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS (10 s) on one cold npm view through the Windows command shell. runNpmUpdateQuery in src/sdk/extension/update-check.ts maps every failure, including that timeout, to the stable code npm_registry_lookup_failed, so neither the nightly log nor a user's pm extension --manage output can tell a slow npm from an unavailable registry. Proposed: report a distinct stable code for a timed-out lookup (killed subprocess with ETIMEDOUT or SIGTERM) without echoing npm's command, stderr or environment, name the budget in the diagnostic, and give the integration test a deterministic registry check budget so Windows cold npm starts do not fail it. Related evidence work: pm-q7c36n kept subprocess timeout and signal evidence for registry install acceptance; pm-2zjs0g measures nightly family rates.

A timed-out npm update lookup reports a distinct stable code (no npm command, stderr or environment in the output) and the diagnostic names the budget; the extension-diagnostic-purity integration test no longer depends on a cold Windows npm start finishing inside 10 s; unit tests cover the timeout and failure classifications
A slow npm view is reported as a timeout distinct from an unavailable registry, and the Windows nightly freshness test is deterministic
Every lookup failure, including the 10 s timeout, is npm_registry_lookup_failed, and the Windows nightly test failed twice at the timeout
